panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: IHC stain for CD20 demonstrates B-cell positivity, supporting the diagnosis of EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcers based on the provided evidence. B: IHC stain for CD30 indicates the presence of CD30 positive cells within the tissue, consistent with the markers used to diagnose EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcers. C: IHC staining for C-myc shows limited expression (<5%), indicating cellular characteristics relevant to the evaluation of EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcers. D: EBER positivity is a key finding presented in the figure, directly supporting the diagnosis of EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcers.

plate_findings.evidence: Left sided facial swelling causing lip droop

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Panel A shows significant facial swelling consistent with the EBVMCU presentation described in the caption, which led to facial distortion. B: Panel B depicts the left palatal ulceration, confirming the EBVMCU diagnosis and showing associated dental loss. C: Panel C shows the ulcer/mass eroding the maxilla and palate, fitting the ulcer definition and describing tissue destruction. D: Panel D demonstrates ulceration confined to the gum line, attributed to EBVMCU. E: Panel E shows mucosal changes (hypertrophy) in the context of the EBVMCU case, indicating chronic inflammation/reaction.
